rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — this is genuinely useful timing. Here's something concrete that fits five hours a week and doesn't depend on anything else being settled yet: Could you help build a short \"landscape map\" of independent AI-safety work? The goal is to figure out what's neglected rather than add to something crowded. Roughly: - What's already being funded/done (newsletters, reading groups, evals efforts, compute-grant programs, policy-comment campaigns, etc.) — a few lines each, with sources. - Where the gaps look real vs. just unglamorous. - Any niches where a small, careful operation (one person, part-time, modest budget) could plausibly add value without duplicating existing efforts. No need to make this polished or public — just a working doc we can both edit. I'll send a shared doc link or you can draft it and send it over, whichever is easier. No rush on a specific date, but even a rough first pass in a couple of weeks would help a lot. Separately: this is all still quiet for now (not publicly announced), so I'd appreciate keeping it low-key for the moment — I'll explain more once a couple of things on my end are settled. Thanks again for offering — really appreciated. Morgan"
rows.quote: Replied to Priya Raman with a concrete task (landscape map of neglected AI-safety work).

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for thinking of Halcyon Threshold — I'm flattered, genuinely. I'm not in a position to go on record by name for a piece like this right now (it's very early days, and I've got some things to sort out on my end before I'm comfortable being quoted in print). I don't want to give you a rushed, half-considered quote either. Happy to stay in touch and reconnect if you're writing something similar down the road. Best, Morgan"
rows.quote: Declined the reporter's (Larkin Dispatch) request to quote you by name

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute, Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold for this. For the moment I'm not in a position to add my name to a signed, press-distributed letter — some things on my end need to be settled first. I'd rather decline than sign and then have to walk it back. I'll keep an eye on the letter's progress, and please feel free to flag future opportunities — this isn't a no forever, just a no for now. Best, Morgan Hale"
rows.quote: Deferred the Corvid Institute open-letter signature for the same reason (soft no, door left open).

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Idris Bellamy <grants@emberfallfund.org> with subject "Re: Rapid grants — yes, you can still apply". It read: "Hi Idris, Thanks for this, and good to meet you too. I'm working through an internal review on my end before I can submit anything that names me as the accountable recipient of grant funds — I'm hoping to have that cleared up soon, but it may land close to or just past the 30th. Two questions: (1) is there any flexibility on the deadline for this round, and (2) if not, is there likely to be a future rapid round I could aim for instead? Either way I'd still like to put together a short proposal — just want to make sure I'm not jumping ahead of myself. Thanks, Morgan"
rows.quote: Told Idris at Emberfall you're mid-"internal review" and asked about deadline flexibility for the rapid grant.
